title: Are dental recall intervals risk-based? A cross-sectional study of records in 14 general dental practices
abstract: Objective: to estimate how often adult recall intervals match recorded risk and independent risk markers, and how often intervals are missing, by area deprivation. Design: cross-sectional study of 1,120 anonymised records from 14 practices in one month of 2027. Results and conclusions will follow extraction.
introduction: Guidance asks for risk-based recall, and randomised evidence suggests longer intervals are safe for low-risk adults, but record studies elsewhere show most adults recalled at six months. Commissioners need a local baseline before contracts change.
methods: Random selection of 80 examination records per practice; extraction of interval, risk field and independent markers; a random-intercept logistic model with practice clustering.
results: No data have been extracted yet. The report will present concordance overall and by practice, missing intervals by deprivation, and risk-field quality.
discussion: The discussion will relate current practice to guidance and contracts and set out what a risk-based contract would need to measure.
limitations: Unreliable recorded risk; one month; 14 practices.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim that longer intervals are safe in this network.
summary: STROBE-structured draft with results left empty.
